# `adi-schedules` — types

> The WORKFLOWS schedule sweep (ADI-MONO-141 §D): computes which slots a workflow's cron rule owes since it was last checked, in the workflow's own IANA timezone with DST handled, collapses a downtime backlog to a single fire (or none, under `catchUp: skip`), and claims each `wf@slot` run key exactly once. Pure library — the workflow engine (WF-5) supplies the schedules and what a pour actually does.

## `src/rule.rs`

### enum `CatchUp`

What happens when more than one slot is due at once — a gap the sweep was down through, not an ordinary tick (exactly one slot due always fires, whatever this is set to; see `crate::slots::due`). Spec section D: "Missed slots after downtime fire ONCE; a per-workflow `catchUp: "skip"` option is available." `CatchUp::Fire` *is* that default "fire once", named for what it does rather than left as the absence of `CatchUp::Skip` — a `catch_up: None` would tempt a match somewhere into reading it as a third state that doesn't exist.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum CatchUp {
    #[default]
    Fire,
    Skip,
}
```

### struct `ScheduleRule`

One workflow's schedule trigger — spec section E's `on: schedule(cron, tz)`. A workflow file may export several (`on: [schedule(...), schedule(...)]`); each becomes its own `ScheduleRule`, sharing nothing with the others but the `workflow` name they both pour runs for.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ScheduleRule {
    pub workflow: String,
    pub cron: String,
    pub tz: String,
    pub catch_up: CatchUp,
}
```
